$comment: Machine-readable feature tracker. See AGENTS.md "Work-in-progress rule" for usage; verify entries with `make verify-feature ID=Fxxx` and mutate state via `make feature-mark`.

wip_rule.description: At most one feature may be in `in_progress` per git branch. Multiple worktrees can each have one in-flight feature.
wip_rule.enforcement: Soft — agents check at session start; not yet a CI gate.

verification_conventions.executable: Shell command that exits 0 on pass and non-zero on fail.
verification_conventions.manual: Verification not yet automated — requires a human or agent to walk a UI flow. `make verify-feature` exits 4 (UNVERIFIED) unless the entry carries a dated receipt: optional `last_verified` (ISO date the flow was last walked) and `verified_by` (verify-skill transcript path or e2e spec path). Add both when marking a manual feature verified.
verification_conventions.null: No verification defined yet. Treat as a gap to fix.

deployment_conventions.migrations: REQUIRED on every entry, in exactly one of three shapes: an array of migration filenames in supabase/migrations/ that this feature needs applied; [] when the entry has been audited and needs no schema change; "unaudited" when nobody has established which it is. Mandatory rather than opt-in so a forgotten field cannot make the gate vacuously pass — and three-valued because a blanket [] backfill is a claim, not an audit, and a false claim a check blesses is worse than an unread one. A declared array names the migration(s) that INTRODUCE the schema the feature depends on (its anchors), not an exhaustive history of every later ALTER that touched the same tables. Every declared name is checked against the real chain, so a renumber/rename fails loudly.
deployment_conventions.deployment: REQUIRED once state is `passing` and `migrations` is a non-empty array. Records SCHEMA APPLICATION only — not that the feature was exercised against production (that stays in `verification` / `last_verified`). Exactly one of two shapes, no other keys: {"state":"live","observed_live_on":"YYYY-MM-DD","verified_by":[...]} or {"state":"pending","pending_since":"YYYY-MM-DD","tracking_issue":NNN}. `observed_live_on` is the date the schema was OBSERVED present on live — an upper bound on the apply date, not the apply date — and must be a real, non-future ISO date. `verified_by` MUST cite supabase/live-catalog.snapshot.txt: the check opens that snapshot and requires every table, function and trigger the declared migrations create to appear in it. The snapshot does not record views, columns or data, so a migration that only adds those is counted as "not verifiable from the snapshot" in the output rather than silently blessed. Other `verified_by` items may be existing repo-relative paths or "#NNN" issue/PR pointers; #NNN is NOT resolved — this check never reaches the network. A `pending` record's `tracking_issue` is unresolved for the same reason, so `pending_since` is the dated receipt that stops it rotting: older than 90 days fails until it is applied or re-confirmed.
deployment_conventions.enforcement: `make check-deploy-state` (part of `make check` and the CI static job) and `make verify-feature ID=Fxxx`; both exit 4 (UNVERIFIED) on a violation. `unaudited_backlog.count` must equal the number of entries declaring "unaudited", so auditing one means lowering it and adding one means raising it visibly in review. Implementation: scripts/check-feature-deployment.ts.

features.title: Error: No QueryClient set, use QueryClientProvider to set one
Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client (culprit: /dashboard)
features.notes: PR #308 already fixed the originally-reported cause (ChatLayout's ChatPanel using next/dynamic(ssr:false)), merged 2026-07-05 — but the issue kept receiving new events afterward (last seen 2026-07-11, in a release that already had that fix). Root cause of the recurrence: TrendChartLazy and BatchActivityHeatmapLazy (src/components/dashboard/) also used next/dynamic({ ssr:false }), and are rendered inside ProductionTrends/SalesTrends, which sit inside a Suspense boundary that itself genuinely suspends (usePeriod() -> useSearchParams()). Nesting a dynamic(ssr:false) client-only bailout boundary inside another suspending boundary is the same class of bug already fixed for ChatLayout. Fix: converted both to React.lazy + an explicit <Suspense> at each call site (4 usages across src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx and src/app/(app)/dashboard/sales/page.tsx), mirroring the established ChatLayout fix. cogs-period-chart-lazy.tsx and batch-readings-chart-lazy.tsx use the same next/dynamic(ssr:false) pattern but are not nested inside a suspending boundary, so left as-is.

features.title: Upsert error for %s batch %d: %s
features.user_visible_behavior: MongoDB sync (POST /api/integrations/mongodb/sync) failed an entire 50-row upsert chunk whenever the source Mongo data had two documents resolving to the same onConflict key (e.g. duplicate beer_styles/brands/vessels names) — Postgres rejects a whole INSERT ... ON CONFLICT statement, not just the offending rows, when two rows in it target the same conflict key.
features.notes: Root cause (2026-07-13, PR #395): upsertRows() (src/integrations/mongodb/sync.ts) sent Mongo-derived rows straight through to a single Supabase .upsert() call per 50-row chunk without deduping by the onConflict column(s) first. Fix added dedupeByConflictKey(), which keeps the last row per conflict-key value (rows missing the conflict column pass through untouched, e.g. recipes upserts with no explicit id) and logs a warning with the dropped count. The Sentry issue kept firing after that fix (36 events through 2026-07-14), so it was re-triaged: classification is (D) observability gap, not a recurrence of the original defect. logger.error("Upsert error for %s batch %d: %s", table, batchIndex, error.message) is a pino printf-style call, but src/lib/logger.ts's forwardToSentry() only handled Error-instance / {err,...ctx}+message / bare-string call shapes — a printf template with substitution args fell into the bare-string branch and was forwarded to Sentry.captureMessage() UN-interpolated, so every event showed the literal template with no table name, batch index, or actual Postgres error message. That is exactly why this session's stack trace was (unavailable) and the event context was empty: the real failure is still unknown. Fixed forwardToSentry() to interpolate printf placeholders via node:util format() before forwarding (covers this and every other printf-style logger.error/fatal call site in the repo), and upgraded the two implicated sync.ts call sites (upsertRows, syncPhase) to structured logger.error({err, ...ctx}, msg) calls so they route to Sentry.captureException with a real stack instead of just a message. Followups: the underlying Postgres error that is still recurring after the 2026-07-13 dedup fix is NOT diagnosed by this session — only its reporting is fixed. The next production event for this issue will carry the real table name, batch index, and Postgres error message (or a full stack via captureException), and should be re-triaged as a fresh (A)/(B) investigation once it arrives. Investigation issue: energee/mgr#433.

features.title: Failed to fetch production trends:
features.user_visible_behavior: The dashboard, sales, and inventory trend sections caught RPC errors (get_production_trends / get_sales_trends / get_inventory_trends) and returned an empty array from the query, so React Query treated the fetch as a success. Users saw a silently zeroed-out empty state (or, on a transient background refetch failure, a chart flip to a misleading zero) with no indication the fetch had failed. Fixed by rethrowing after logging so isError surfaces, and rendering an explicit "Couldn't load ... trends" DashboardEmpty state only when there is no cached data to fall back on (preserves last known-good data across transient refetchInterval polling failures).
features.notes: Pattern scan found the identical swallow-and-return-[] bug duplicated in all three dashboard trend queries (dashboard/page.tsx ProductionTrends, dashboard/inventory/page.tsx InventoryTrends, dashboard/sales/page.tsx SalesTrends); all three fixed identically.

features.title: Failed to fetch planned batches by day:
features.user_visible_behavior: BatchActivityHeatmap on /dashboard logged RPC errors by passing a destructured plain object to log.error instead of the real PostgrestError instance, so client-logger's instanceof-Error check missed it and Sentry captured only the generic literal message with no stack or detail. Same anti-pattern found and fixed in NotificationsProvider's fetch-notifications error path.

features.title: Failed to fetch notifications:
features.user_visible_behavior: Second recurrence of this Sentry issue, different root cause than the first. On /sales/customers/:id (dev environment), NotificationsProvider's unread-notifications fetch failed with a browser-level "TypeError: Failed to fetch" while calling the Supabase REST endpoint. Classified (D) observability gap: postgrest-js's fetch `.catch()` handler wraps network-level failures (and some Postgrest error responses) as a plain object literal `{ message, details, hint, code }` that is NOT an `instanceof Error`, despite its `PostgrestError` TS type claiming otherwise, so client-logger.ts's `instanceof Error` check missed it and Sentry got a stack-less captureMessage instead of the real message/stack/code. Fixed client-logger.ts to also recognize and unwrap Postgrest-error-shaped plain objects into a real Error (preserving message, stack from `details`, and code/hint as extra) before forwarding to Sentry.captureException — this applies to every log.error/log.warn call site in the app, not just notifications. The underlying network failure itself (why the fetch to Supabase failed) is still unresolved infra/(B) and is tracked in a separate GitHub issue, since it isn't fixable from application code. First recurrence (lock-steal AbortError from a non-singleton browser client) was fixed separately — see notes.
features.notes: History: first occurrence fixed by making src/lib/supabase/client.ts's createClient() a module-scoped singleton (lock-steal AbortError root cause). This second occurrence is a different symptom (network-level fetch failure) that exposed a pre-existing observability gap in client-logger.ts; see GitHub issue #514 for the still-unresolved network failure.

features.title: Hydration Error (culprit: /dashboard)
features.notes: This issue ID has a three-act history on /dashboard: PR #297 fixed a prefill-store sessionStorage read happening during render; PR #306 fixed unpinned toLocaleDateString()/toLocaleString() locale mismatches; the issue kept recurring afterward (last seen 2026-07-11T02:25:44Z, release 00fbe79). features.title: Error: Attempted to call createRevisionHistoryDisplay() from the server but createRevisionHistoryDisplay is on the client.
features.user_visible_behavior: While developing the sitewide server-prefetch loading pattern, importing an assembled entity presentation (e.g. batchEntity) from a Server Component crashed: createRevisionHistoryDisplay() is invoked eagerly at module scope inside every entity presentation.tsx, and its defining file carried an unnecessary "use client" directive even though it uses no hooks itself (the real hook logic lives in the child RevisionHistory component, which already has its own directive). Removed the incorrect directive so the factory can be called safely regardless of which context imports the presentation module. The same eagerly-invoked-factory-in-a-"use client"-file pattern existed for createQBOSyncDisplay (used by customer/supplier/order/purchase-order presentations); extracted it into a new non-client qbo-sync-display.tsx, mirroring the existing revision-history split, so QBOSyncSection keeps its (genuinely required) "use client" directive in its own file.

features.title: Error: Attempted to call createRevisionHistoryDisplay() from the server but createRevisionHistoryDisplay is on the client.
features.user_visible_behavior: Dev-only /_error crash on /production/batches (5 events, 2026-07-15T06:00-06:05Z, release 492ff277, worktree loading-pattern). A prior revision of production/batches/loading.tsx imported the assembled batchEntity from '@/entities/batch' (a client module) instead of the server-safe batchCore, purely to read listColumns.length for a skeleton. presentation.tsx calls the client-only factory createRevisionHistoryDisplay("batches") at module-evaluation top level (exported by a "use client" file), so evaluating that import chain in the server module graph threw exactly this error.
features.notes: Root cause already fixed on main before this harness run: commit c6b5539 (PR #453, authored 2026-07-15T07:11:53Z — after the last Sentry event at 06:05:31Z) rewrote loading.tsx to render null instead of importing batchEntity. Verified current production/batches/loading.tsx, page.tsx, and every other src/app server file import only *Core (server-safe) modules or @/entities/cores, never an assembled client entity config. No code fix was needed; added a regression test (server-entity-import-boundary.test.ts) that statically walks every non-"use client" file under src/app and fails if any imports an assembled @/entities/<name> config, so this class of RSC-boundary violation can't silently reappear. Confirmed the test fails against the exact pre-fix loading.tsx content and passes on current main.
